evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Places Pygame on the library / framework / engine ladder, explains what that trade-off buys and costs, and identifies SDL as the C layer underneath.

Pygame is a library, not an engine: it supplies primitives while the loop and structure are the developer's. -- Confirmed -- borne out by the whole chapter: loop, collisions and architecture are all hand-written in 20.2/20.21/20.26.
Pygame is built on SDL (Simple DirectMedia Layer), written in C. -- Confirmed -- `pygame.version.SDL` reports 2.32.10 and the banner prints 'pygame-ce 2.5.8 (SDL 2.32.10, Python 3.14.6)'.

Flask (chapter 23) illustrates the framework tier. -- Was false -- Flask is chapter 22 («Основы веб-разработки», 190 mentions); chapter 23 is the SafeSort project with zero Flask mentions. Fixed under F-008.

Core concepts transfer to larger engines, though architecture and APIs differ. -- Confirmed, and notably well hedged -- the callout explicitly lists what does *not* transfer (physics timestep, scene model, collision system), the honest version of a claim usually made too broadly.
